# Declared inventory of the hosted app's Fly secrets — the managing-source of truth.
#
# Contract (enforced by .github/scripts/check-fly-secret-drift.py, issue #4126):
#   every name returned by `flyctl secrets list -a tortoise-y4mjjq` MUST appear
#   here, and its source MUST describe what keeps it in sync. A name that exists
#   only on Fly is drift by construction: it survives every deploy unversioned,
#   nobody can rotate it from GitHub, and CI cannot see it.
#
# Issue #4126 paid for this: `TORTOISE_SESSION_LLM_MODEL` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
# were hand-set on the Fly app with no managing source, the deployed key 403'd on
# every extraction call, and production answered 200 with `status: "partial"` /
# `extracted: 0` for 50/50 sessions — a total extraction outage no gate could see.
#
# FORMAT — `<NAME> <source>`, one per line. `#` comments and blank lines ignored.
#
# ⛔ A `gh-secret:<GH_NAME>` LINE MUST HAVE A MATCHING PROBE LINE in
#    deploy-hosted.yml's `GH_SECRETS_PRESENT` block. No CI token can list
#    repository secrets, so the deploy states which ones it carries; that is what
#    lets the gate fail on a declaration whose GitHub secret does not exist (the
#    #4126 incident: the guarded propagation was a permanent no-op and Fly kept a
#    hand-managed value). A name the probe omits reads as ABSENT, so a forgotten
#    line FAILS the deploy for that name rather than passing it — fail-closed, and
#    it names the exact variable to fix.
#
#   gh-secret:<GH_NAME>  propagated by .github/workflows/deploy-hosted.yml from
#                        the GitHub Actions secret <GH_NAME> (not always the same
#                        name — e.g. GITHUB_CLIENT_ID ← GH_CLIENT_ID). Verified
#                        both ways: a declaration the workflow no longer
#                        references is a violation, so this file cannot rot.
#   workflow             set by the workflow from non-secret context
#                        (${GITHUB_SHA}, a composed feature flag).
#   fly-toml-env         applied from fly.toml `[env]` — versioned, and the
#                        deploy applies it, so no Fly secret needs to exist.
#                        THREE states FAIL this declaration: the name is not an
#                        assigned key in fly.toml's `[env]` table; the deploy
#                        ASSIGNS the name (creating the secret that would shadow
#                        the versioned value); and a Fly secret of that name still
#                        EXISTS (the versioned value is not what the app reads).
#                        The last two are the same shadow, and the third is a
#                        TRANSITION rather than drift — the route (b) block below
#                        is the order that completes it, and it says which deploy
#                        may run while the state holds.
#   unmanaged            present on Fly with NO managing source. **This FAILS
#                        the gate** — it is the #4126 defect, not benign debt.
#                        The token names the state precisely so the failure is
#                        actionable: declare the real source
#                        (gh-secret:<GH_NAME> | workflow | fly-toml-env), or
#                        record the value in version control and drop the Fly
#                        secret. A gate that passes on a Fly-only variable is
#                        the fail-open #4126 was filed to close.
#   fly-only:<issue-ref> a DELIBERATELY out-of-band secret: it is managed
#                        outside BOTH GitHub and fly.toml on purpose, and the
#                        named issue carries the recorded decision (its
#                        `OVERRIDES:` marker states what the ruling overrides
#                        and why). `unmanaged` means "nobody declared a source";
#                        this token means "a source was deliberately refused,
#                        and here is the ruling". NOT a synonym for
#                        `unmanaged`: a bare `unmanaged` entry still FAILS the
#                        gate.
#                        The ref must be a WELL-FORMED, non-zero issue number —
#                        `<#N>` for this repo, or `<owner>/<repo>#<N>` for one
#                        elsewhere. `#0`, a non-ASCII digit (`\d` matches
#                        Arabic-Indic numerals), `#`, `#abc`, `#661abc`, `661`
#                        and a bare `owner/repo` are ALL a manifest the checker
#                        cannot read: exit 2, fail-closed, never a pass. The
#                        exception is only meaningful because of the issue it
#                        names, so an entry that names none is `unmanaged` in
#                        disguise.
#                        ⚠️ SHAPE ONLY: the checker is hermetic and offline, so
#                        it verifies the ref is a well-formed issue number — NOT
#                        that the issue exists or carries the ruling. A
#                        well-formed ref to a nonexistent issue passes; the
#                        existence half is a reviewer's job, and the `OVERRIDES:`
#                        marker on the named issue is what makes it checkable.
#                        Also FAILS a declaration whose name is not on Fly
#                        (there is nothing out-of-band to except), whose name
#                        the deploy assigns, or whose name is an assigned key in
#                        `fly.toml [env]` (version-controlled there, and a Fly
#                        secret would shadow that value — the same state the
#                        `fly-toml-env` route rejects).
#                        RESERVED for a decision that says the ABSENCE of a
#                        version-control source IS the property — currently the
#                        one name below, #661 ("never present in GH (operator
#                        out-of-band), so registry content confidentiality does
#                        not inherit the GH trust boundary"). Adopting the
#                        gate's default there would reverse that decision; the
#                        route is to reopen #661, not to drop this token.
#
# ROTATION: for a `gh-secret:` name, rotating the GitHub secret is the only step —
# the next deploy propagates it.
#
# ── ENTRY-POINT FOR A REVIEWER: every name below now names a managing source;
#    the recorded debt is closed (#4471). The one name that is NOT managed from
#    version control is `REGISTRY_STREAM_KEY` at the bottom, declared
#    `fly-only:#661` — read that block and #661's `OVERRIDES:` marker before
#    touching it, and treat a new `fly-only:` entry as needing an owner decision,
#    not a convenience spelling.

# ── Managed from GitHub Actions secrets (deploy-hosted.yml) ───────────────────
FASTAPI_INTERNAL_KEY            gh-secret:FASTAPI_INTERNAL_KEY
TORTOISE_SECRET_PEPPER          gh-secret:TORTOISE_SECRET_PEPPER

# #4126: a deliberate flash-class override for session-capture extraction. The
# value is a model id, not a credential, so it is recorded in the deploy
# definition itself (`.github/workflows/deploy-hosted.yml`) and assigned
# UNCONDITIONALLY there — a GitHub secret may still override it. That is the fix
# for the #4126 half where "the GitHub secret is absent" and "deliberately using
# the default" were indistinguishable: the default is now explicit and versioned
# (`openrouter:google/gemini-2.5-flash`), and the deploy overwrites whichever
# value was hand-set on Fly.
TORTOISE_SESSION_LLM_MODEL      workflow

# ── Assigned by the workflow, not currently present on Fly ────────────────────
# The deploy sets each of these on Fly once its GitHub secret exists (an
# alternate LLM provider, the #2318 backup-key rotation window, a custom
# transactional sender, Turnstile). They are declared so the gate cannot
# hard-fail the NEXT deploy after someone first sets one: the run that sets it
# passes (the guard runs before the propagation step) and every run after would
# report an undeclared Fly name. Declaring them is the reverse half of the
# contract — a Fly variable the workflow can assign must have a declaration.
RESEND_FROM_EMAIL              gh-secret:RESEND_FROM_EMAIL
BILLING_FROM_EMAIL              gh-secret:BILLING_FROM_EMAIL
OPENAI_API_KEY                  gh-secret:OPENAI_API_KEY
GEMINI_API_KEY                  gh-secret:GEMINI_API_KEY
TORTOISE_BACKUP_KEY_PREVIOUS    gh-secret:TORTOISE_BACKUP_KEY_PREVIOUS
BACKUP_SIMULATE_ENABLED         gh-secret:BACKUP_SIMULATE_ENABLED
TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY            gh-secret:TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY

# ── Set by the workflow from non-secret context ───────────────────────────────
TORTOISE_GIT_SHA                workflow   # ${GITHUB_SHA}; recorded per deploy
BACKUP_SWEEP_ENABLED            workflow   # composed from the backup/R2/DR secret set

# ── Adopted from the Fly-only hand-set set under #4126 ────────────────────────
# Both already exist as GitHub Actions secrets, so declaring them here makes the
# deploy the managing source: the value on Fly stops being hand-set, and a
# rotation from GitHub is the only step needed for it to take effect.
# NOTE: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY ← SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY — the GitHub secret has
# the legacy name; the Fly variable keeps the RuntimeEnv name the app reads
# (tools/capture_cost_report.py accepts either, tortoise/ reads the *_ROLE_* one).
SUPABASE_URL                    gh-secret:SUPABASE_URL
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY       gh-secret:SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY

# ── Resolved under #4126 — the seven recorded-debt names ─────────────────────
# #4126's acceptance was that the deploy gate FAILS on this state, so the gate
# was correct to be red; it is the STATE that is fixed, not the gate. Six of the
# seven were convergent fixes (there was no decision to make): a non-secret
# config value belongs in version-controlled env, a secret belongs in CI
# secrets. The seventh is a recorded decision and gets its own category.
#
# CONFIG (non-secret) — route (b): the value's home is `fly.toml [env]` (the
# deploy applies it — versioned — and no Fly secret then needs to exist), and the
# Fly secret of the same name is UNSET
# (`flyctl secrets unset <NAME> --app tortoise-y4mjjq`).
#
# ⛔ WRITE PRODUCTION'S CURRENT VALUE, NEVER `.env.example`'s DEFAULT. The `[env]`
# value becomes effective the moment the secret is unset — until then the secret
# SHADOWS it and nothing you deploy for it is observable — so the value written
# here is the value production then runs. Confirm the live effective value first
# (#4471's caution for whoever executes this route). The `.env.example` vs live
# `0`/`1` divergence on `TORTOISE_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED` is the general case,
# not a one-off.
#
# ⛔ `fly.toml` IS THE ONLY DURABLE HOME. The deploy re-materialises the machine's
# env from `fly.toml`, so any `[env]` value that is not in the MERGED `fly.toml`
# is removed by the next `deploy-hosted` run — with no gate, warning or test to
# say so (#4568). Never set the value out-of-band (`secrets set` / `machine
# update`), and never deploy a PRE-merge `fly.toml`: step 1 below is merged first.
#
# ⛔ ORDER MATTERS — THE `[env]` VALUE MUST BE ON THE MACHINE BEFORE THE UNSET.
# While the secret exists THIS gate fails the name — `declared fly-toml-env but is
# also a Fly secret` — exit 1, before `flyctl deploy` runs, so a push-triggered
# deploy is RED on this name and cannot apply `[env]` unless a bypass is armed —
# and the only lane a push run has is the PERSISTENT repo variable, which this
# transition must not use (it would stay set). No other declaration survives that
# either (`unmanaged` → UNSOURCED; no entry → UNDECLARED; `fly-only:#N` →
# rejected for an `[env]` key; `gh-secret:` → needs a GitHub secret that does not
# exist for a value living only on Fly, and creating one is route (a), not route
# (b)). So:
#   1. land the `[env]` entry at production's CURRENT value (see the ⛔ above)
#      + this declaration, merged;
#   2. apply `[env]` with a `deploy-hosted` dispatch OF THE MERGED COMMIT
#      carrying the PER-RUN input `skip-fly-secret-provenance: true` (an
#      exit-1-class bypass, reported in the run summary). Use the dispatch INPUT,
#      never the repo variable — the input is consumed by the run, so nothing is
#      left set. CONFIRM THIS NAME'S SHADOW IS THE ONLY VIOLATION: the bypass
#      releases EVERY exit-1 violation in the run, and the summary names the
#      gate, not the violations (they are in the step log). The secret still
#      shadows `[env]`, so the value the app reads does not change. (A config-
#      only operator deploy of the current image — how #4523 did it — also
#      applies `[env]`, but runs none of the deploy gates and leaves no run
#      summary or audit line: this dispatch is the route.)
#   3. WAIT FOR THE DEPLOY JOB, NOT THE RUN — a `deploy-hosted` RUN can end RED
#      with `[env]` already applied: since #4538 the separate, fail-closed
#      `post-deploy-verify` job fails AFTER `flyctl deploy` succeeded, and
#      `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` can cancel a run after that step too.
#      So require the `deploy-api` job's Deploy step to succeed — unsetting
#      against a deploy that did NOT apply `[env]` drops the value. Only then:
#      `flyctl secrets unset <NAME> --app tortoise-y4mjjq`;
#   4. verify BOTH: `flyctl secrets list -a tortoise-y4mjjq` must no longer list
#      `<NAME>` (the shadow is gone — this list is the gate's own input), AND
#      `printenv <NAME>` on the machine must still return the value from step 1
#      (the move is behaviour-preserving). Neither alone is enough: `secrets
#      list` says nothing about the value, and `printenv` alone cannot say WHICH
#      source supplied it.
#
# The order relies on Fly applying `[env]` at deploy and preserving the machine
# config across a `secrets unset`; nothing asserts the running env (that is
# #4568's other half), so step 4 is the only check on the outcome — run both
# halves. A push-triggered deploy between (1) and (3) is red on this name BY
# DESIGN (the transitional state is the one the gate cannot express), so finish
# (3) as soon as step 2's Deploy step succeeds — and do NOT clear that freeze with
# `vars.SKIP_FLY_SECRET_PROVENANCE`, which leaves the incident-class lane armed.
#
# ⛔ WHY THE MERGED COMMIT — the #4568 evidence. A PRE-merge `[env]` application
# was removed by the next `deploy-hosted` run re-applying `main`'s `fly.toml`
# (which lacked the entries), and the value stayed ABSENT for ~5 h
# (TORTOISE_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED flipped off). Unset-first reaches that same
# absent state directly, with no revert needed.
#
# `TORTOISE_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED` moved as the LIVE value (`1`), not
# `.env.example`'s documented dev default (`0`) — the move is
# behaviour-preserving and the flag's value remains the owner's call.
TORTOISE_CONTROL_PLANE          fly-toml-env
TORTOISE_REAUTH_WINDOW_SECONDS  fly-toml-env
TORTOISE_MANUAL_LINKING_ENABLED fly-toml-env
# SECRETS — route (a): adopted by the deploy. The GitHub Actions secret was
# created from the LIVE Fly value (the value never entered a log or a
# transcript), the propagation line was added to deploy-hosted.yml, and the
# matching GH_SECRETS_PRESENT probe line was added with it (a `gh-secret:`
# declaration with no probe line reads as ABSENT and fails the deploy).
TORTOISE_AUDIT_DSN              gh-secret:TORTOISE_AUDIT_DSN   # Supabase pooler DSN (audit_events; #669/#771)
TORTOISE_LINK_INTENT_SECRET     gh-secret:TORTOISE_LINK_INTENT_SECRET   # HMAC key for link-intent refs (#1765)
SENTRY_DSN                      gh-secret:SENTRY_DSN   # error tracking; activates only when set

# ── Decision-backed exception: deliberately Fly-only (NOT `unmanaged`) ───────
# #661 is a CLOSED recorded decision: this key must be "never present in GH
# (operator out-of-band), so registry content confidentiality does not inherit
# the GH trust boundary", with its own E2E — "a GH workflow cannot decrypt a
# registry archive with the Fly-only key". Its `OVERRIDES:` marker is on #661.
# Moving it into a GitHub secret would REVERSE that security decision; retiring
# it would break registry streaming. So it is neither — it is declared, and the
# issue carries the ruling. Rotation stays out-of-band:
#   tools/rotate-backup-keys.py --role registry_stream
REGISTRY_STREAM_KEY             fly-only:#661
